{
  "decision_type": "stop",
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "The model exploits trial-specific signatures (e.g., task direction) that transfer to new trials within the same subject/session.",
      "mechanism": "Task-level information shared across windows of a single trial allows generalization from training windows to test windows on unseen trials, driving high window split performance despite no true signal in random labels.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": ["obs_1", "req_2"],
      "limitations": "Does not rule out subject-specific mappings or identity effects."
    },
    {
      "id": "H3",
      "claim": "The model exploits session identities (domain/collection effects) rather than trial content.",
      "mechanism": "Labels are partially determined by the session ID, allowing high performance when test data shares these IDs with training data. Note: Window and Trial splits share all 32 sessions; Subject split has no session overlap.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": ["obs_1", "req_2"],
      "limitations": "Does not rule out trial-specific signatures."
    }
  ],
  "reason": "Both H1 and H3 are supported by evidence. Trial shuffling (H1) broke performance, while session-based effects (H3) remain plausible but less likely given the lack of subject overlap in other splits.",
  "final_judgment": "The model exploits trial-specific signatures rather than session identities or subject mappings.",
  "evidence_ids": ["obs_1", "req_2"],
  "remaining_uncertainty": null,
  "reasoning_summary": "Trial shuffling broke performance (H1 supported). Session identity unlikely as primary driver given lack of robust signal in other splits. Conclusion: Trial-specific signatures drive model behavior."
}
